title: Engineering Production Systems for an Agentic Era: QCon San Francisco 2026
gist: Promotional preview of QCon San Francisco 2026 sessions on running AI agents in production: Airbnb's support-agent guardrails, OpenAI's claim of $100M ARR for OpenAI Ads in under six weeks, Netflix compression trade-offs, and Honeycomb's MCP used by over 40% of weekly active users.

insights.claim: AI agents are becoming users of production systems, initiating customer actions, querying observability data, and influencing how software is tested and released, which raises questions about delegation, evidence before production, and retained human control.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Demand is shifting toward guardrail, observability and agent-readiness tooling, not just code generation.
insights.quote: AI agents are changing more than the way code is written. They are becoming users of production systems

insights.claim: The QCon San Francisco 2026 program (November 16-20) brings practitioners from Airbnb, OpenAI, Netflix, Honeycomb and others to share production answers to agent-era engineering questions, with the focus on decisions teams are already making rather than what agents may eventually do.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Signals which companies are positioned as credible production-agent adopters.

insights.claim: An agent that can take action on a customer's account carries materially higher risk than one that only drafts text, so controls must go beyond a prompt or a single model-level safeguard.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Action-taking agents need layered safety spend; watch vendors selling guardrails and testing.
insights.locator: Moving AI agents into customer-facing systems

insights.claim: Airbnb's customer support agent serves millions of customers, maintains context across conversations and can initiate account actions, and is protected by layered controls: input sanitization, classifiers, shadow testing, false-positive management and rapid-response mitigations.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Gives a concrete template of the guardrail stack large consumer platforms use before agent launch.
insights.locator: In "How Airbnb Guardrailed Its AI Customer Support Agent"

insights.claim: Coding agents cut implementation and iteration time, but speed does not remove the need for engineering judgment; teams must still decide how generated work is verified and who owns architecture, quality and release.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Productivity gains are bounded by verification and ownership, tempering pure headcount-reduction narratives.
insights.locator: Deciding what coding agents should and should not own

insights.claim: OpenAI Ads was built with coding agents from the start and scaled to more than $100 million in annual recurring revenue in under six weeks, according to the session description by OpenAI's Brian Yang.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Claimed ads ramp is a datapoint for OpenAI monetization and for agent-accelerated product development, though it is a self-reported conference abstract.
insights.locator: Brian Yang, Member of Technical Staff at OpenAI

insights.claim: The OpenAI session will cover feedback loops, verification, token economics and the decisions that remained under human ownership, framing token cost as a design variable in agent-built products.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Token economics is becoming a first-order operating consideration for agent-heavy teams.
insights.locator: The session will cover feedback loops

insights.claim: Optimizing one part of a distributed system can create costs elsewhere, especially at high request volumes, so AI-era teams still face latency, capacity, compatibility, failure-handling and safe-rollout problems.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Infrastructure efficiency gains require system-wide evaluation; classic reliability skills stay valuable.
insights.locator: Understanding system-wide AI trade-offs at scale

insights.claim: Netflix engineers Joseph Lynch and Ayushi Singh will treat adaptive compression for key-value storage as a systems problem spanning billions of daily requests and petabytes of data, weighing storage footprint, cache behavior, network I/O, p99 latency, dictionary versioning, compatibility and rollout safety.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Illustrates the scale at which Netflix tunes storage cost against tail latency.

insights.claim: An API can be technically accessible to an agent without being understandable enough to produce reliable results, so production systems must communicate intent, context and constraints to non-human users.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Agent-legible interfaces (schemas, descriptions) become a product differentiator for software vendors.
insights.locator: Making production systems understandable to agents

insights.claim: Honeycomb's observability MCP server is used by more than 40% of its weekly active users to run production queries through agents, per Technical Fellow Liz Fong-Jones' session description.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Strong early adoption evidence that agent interfaces to observability data gain real usage; positive read for MCP-style integrations.
insights.quote: an MCP server used by more than 40% of Honeycomb’s weekly active users
insights.locator: Making Production Legible to Agents session

insights.claim: Lessons from the Honeycomb MCP cover token economy, tool descriptions, schemas, evaluations, output formats and defects found in real use, and are said to apply beyond observability to reduce ambiguity in agent actions.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Checklist for evaluating how agent-ready a vendor's tooling is.
insights.locator: The session will cover token economy

insights.claim: InfoQ is pairing QCon SF with a four-day Certified Architect Program (ICSAET certification, workshop led by Luca Mezzalira on November 19) and optional training on November 19-20 covering agent SDK selection, harness engineering, Claude Code and Codex, and AI-assisted coding workflows, with early-bird tickets at $2,955 through October 13.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Training topics show where enterprise upskilling demand is concentrated: agent harnesses and coding-agent tools.
insights.locator: Applying the conference to current architecture decisions
